name: Woodcut / Linocut
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference grouping two distinct processes by their carved-print look. Use directional cut marks, bold positive-negative shapes, and form-following hatching. Woodcut may emphasize grain; linocut may use clean carved masses. Grain is not a canonical requirement.
suitableUses: Single striking images, product or editorial introductions, illustrated explanations, folk tales, heritage stories, book trailers, campaign statements, and documentary title cards. Chaptered video or scroll narratives suit meaningful story progression. These are stated fits; choose based on the subject.
limitations: Avoid uniform noise in place of carving marks, inconsistent character carvings, soft paper washes, or extra hues where monochrome is required. Omit chapter transitions when boundaries add no meaning, obscure causality, break a continuous shot or loop, or replace explanation with spectacle. Distinct styles should retain their material rules.
palette: For new artwork without approved colors, suggested tokens are paper #F2E6CA and dark ink #262820: a two-color monochrome pair with no gradient or accent hues. These are suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, and asset colors exactly; use hatching or opacity for tone. Check actual composited text contrast; the stated 12.047 ratio applies only to opaque token pairs.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal print regions or alternate designed print frames; keep cut marks directional. For stories, use deliberate holds and chapter handoffs or progress-linked states with synchronized copy. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to chapters and restore states on reverse scroll; provide keyboard, touch, static or reduced-motion behavior as applicable. Video uses seekable composition time, not live input. Verify direct, backward, and out-of-order seeks; preserve loop seams and avoid generic bounce or smoothing.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping or competing vocals, and synchronize and inspect audio with picture.
assetRequirements: Create directional carved paths, positive-negative masks, and fixed block texture; use designed print frames for pose changes. SVG is recommended for scalable marks, masks and clips. Python and Pillow may preprocess masks, crops, composites or textures. Asset sourcing, exact copy, dimensions, fonts and audio inputs are unspecified; preserve supplied materials and seed or cache stateful generation.
combinations: Works alone for a striking image. With style-030, use monochrome character-led story scenes, consistent carvings, and reading holds; exclude its warm palette and washes. With style-093, reveal monochrome carved display headlines in reading order, use real fonts for small text, and avoid glyph deformation, per-letter springs, and wood-grain text. Supporting styles must respect carving marks.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion method for style, action and fidelity first; SVG is recommended and Motion is optional, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is primary for composition, timing, synchronization, validation and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required limitation exists, recording why. Keep visual and motion logic separate, deterministic and seekable. For HTML scroll patterns, GSAP can map finite progress; PixiJS or tldraw are optional role-specific tools, not required bundles or video renderers. Validate representative frames, full playback, text, dimensions, frame rate, audio sync and loop continuity.
